title: stratified-qos-experiments-journal
content:
Context and motivation:
- We're seeing increasing variance in tail latency and per-request token cost across workloads. Customers want predictable service tiers (SLA for latency and cost bounds) but also want best-effort quality when allowed.
- Hypothesis: introducing stratified QoS lanes + lightweight probabilistic response pruning (and optional fidelity downgrades) will reduce p95 latency and cost while maintaining acceptable perceived quality for most interactive flows.

Problem statement:
- Hosted API currently has single routing policy: lowest compatible model variant by cost/perf with autoscaling. No explicit QoS lanes. During spikes, p95 latency and token cost spike; heavier customers degrade experience for lighter ones.
- Need an experiment framework to evaluate: per-customer QoS lanes (gold/silver/bronze), admission control, probabilistic pruning of generation candidate tokens, and dynamic fidelity downgrades (shorter max tokens / reduced sampling diversity).

Goals / success criteria:
- Primary: Reduce p95 latency by >= 25% under mixed workload stress while keeping mean quality loss (human-rated) < 7% for gold and < 12% for silver in targeted scenarios.
- Secondary: Reduce average token cost for bronze lane by >= 30% with automated fallbacks. Maintain <0.5% increase in API error rate.

User personas and stories:
- Small SaaS startup (developer tier): wants low cost and is ok with occasional shorter/less creative responses. "As an app developer on the free tier, I want my assistant responses to be fast and cheap, even if they are slightly less verbose so I can stay within budget."
- Mid-market product with conversational UI: requires predictable p95 latency < 350ms and high fidelity for paid tier. "As a product engineer on paid plan, I want guaranteed latency and fidelity SLAs so customer UX is consistent."
- Internal ML research team: wants to run experiments on fidelity tradeoffs for instruction-heavy prompts. "As a researcher, I want to be able to enable fidelity mode toggles and capture both token-level and human evaluation metrics for analysis."

Proposed features / knobs:
- QoS lanes: gold / silver / bronze. Mapping rules: per-api-key tag, per-customer profile, or per-route override.
- Admission controller: queue-length-aware throttling with lane priority and soft-budgets (per-minute token budgets).
- Fidelity tiers: full-fidelity, reduced-sampling (temperature clamp, top-k/top-p adjustments), truncated-max-length.
- Probabilistic pruning: on-the-fly pruning of low-probability next-token branches (beam-lite) to save compute; implement as adjustable pruning rate per lane.
- Prefetch + cached prefixes: for bronze, offer prefix caching and precomputed concise recaps to avoid regenerating long contexts.
- Observability: per-lane metrics (latency p50/p95/p99, avg tokens, token cost, error rate, human quality delta), surfaced on Console.

Experiment matrix (initial):
- Matrix axes: lane (gold/silver/bronze) x pruning rate (0%, 10%, 30%) x sampling policy (full, temp=0.7, temp=0.3) x max-length cap (unbounded, -25%, -50%).
- Keep traffic split: 70% control (current behavior), 30% experiment distributed evenly across combinations for that 30%.
- Per-customer sticky assignment: choose low-risk internal Canary customers plus synthetic load.

Measurement plan:
- Automated metrics: p50/p95/p99 generation latency, avg tokens per response, tokens billed, infra GPU utilization, per-request cost estimate.
- Quality metrics: automatic heuristics (BLEU/ROUGE/useful for short tasks not ideal), plus human eval panel rated on 1-5 scale for clarity, relevance, and helpfulness. Collect N=500 samples per lane/variant for initial run.
- Uptime/error: record error class rates (model OOM, timeouts, 5xx).

Implementation notes / architecture interaction:
- Serving runtime changes: need lightweight hook for per-request fidelity policy that adjusts decoding parameters and max token budget before token generation loop. Ideally a single config struct passed into runtime; minimal code path changes.
- Admission controller lives at router: must respect lane priority but allow configurable leak rates to avoid starvation.
- KV/prefix cache: bronze lane should consult a concise-summary cache before generation; store precomputed short recaps (~50-120 tokens) for common prefixes.
- Billing + telemetry: tag telemetry with lane and variant id (experiment id) to attribute cost and quality.

Risk analysis and mitigations:
- Risk: degraded perceived quality may cause churn. Mitigation: only assign low-revenue or opt-in customers to bronze experiments; provide explicit opt-out and visible "economy mode" indicator in response metadata and Console.
- Risk: complexity in routing + debugging. Mitigation: strict feature flags, rollout pipeline with observability, and canary to SRE on-call.
- Risk: billing mismatches. Mitigation: run side-by-side cost simulator to validate billing before public rollout.

UX / API sketches:
- API extension (opt-in): QoS header: X-Redwood-QoS: gold|silver|bronze or qos_profile:q123. Response metadata: qos_applied, pruning_rate, final_sampling_policy, tokens_billed_estimate.
- Console: per-API-key QoS assignment UI + heatmap view for lane-specific tail latency and cost.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How do we measure subjective quality for long-form creative outputs reliably at scale? Human eval is slow and expensive; need sampling heuristics.
- For bronze lane, should we prefer summary-first UX (return concise recap + "expand" toggle) rather than degrade generation by default?
- What are sensible defaults for pruning rates that balance compute savings and quality?

Next steps / short-term plan (2-week sprint):
1) Spike: implement request-level fidelity flag in runtime that can clamp temperature, top-k/top-p, and max_new_tokens. (owner: infra)
2) Router: add QoS header passthrough and per-key mapping config prototype. (owner: platform)
3) Quick experiment harness: small traffic split + telemetry tags; build analysis notebook to compute p95 and token cost deltas. (owner: product + analytics)
4) Human eval plan: define 3 canonical prompt families (faq answer, short creative, summary) and recruit 500 raters from internal + contracted pool. (owner: research)
5) Design Console mock: simple toggle to opt-in particular API keys into bronze lane and view metrics. (owner: DX)

Parking lot / ideas to revisit:
- Slot-based batching for bronze lane to maximize GPU throughput while preserving latency SLAs for gold.
- Preemptive small-answer service (tiny LLM) for super-short queries to avoid invoking full model.
- Per-route micro SLAs: allow product owners to define explicit per-route token budgets and cost caps.

Quick todos (bullet):
- [ ] Create JIRA epic and link to this doc.
- [ ] Wireframe Console assignment UX.
- [ ] Run initial 10% internal-only experiment with 3 pruning rates.
- [ ] Draft customer-facing doc for "economy mode" behavior and opt-in.

Notes to self:
- Keep experiment names consistent: use `sqe-` prefix (stratified-qos-experiment).
- When running human eval, always record prompt seeding to reproduce.

End of journal entry.
